sentences.text: JUDGMENT

The Police Inspector of Vyalikaval police station has filed the charge sheet against the 3 accused persons before learned 8th ACMM Court, Bangalore, alleging the offences punishable u/Sec. 365 of IPC.
2.

After filing of the charge sheet, the Learned Magistrate took cognizance for the offences punishable u/Sec. 395 of IPC against the accused and registered the criminal case bearing CC.No.22537/2012.
3.
The accused were on bail when the charge sheet was filed.

After securing the presence of the accused , the Learned Magistrate had complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.207 of Cr.P.C., by furnishing the copy of charge sheet and other papers annexed with the charge sheet to the accused.

4. Since the offences alleged against the accused punishable u/Sec. 395 of IPC are exclusively triable by the court of Sessions, the Learned Magistrate had committed the S.C.No.260/2019 case to Hon'ble City Civil and Sessions Court, Bengaluru for trial by exercising the power u/Sec.209 of Cr.P.C.
5.

sentences.text: After committal of the case, SC.No.37/2013 was registered against the accused No.1 Vinod and A2 Subramanya and A3 Prabhu and made over to this court.
Since A2 Subramanya was absconding a split up case in SC No. 376/2015 was registered against A2 Subramanya,
Then the matter was posted for hearing the accused on charge.
6. The Accused were heard on the charge.

Since there are sufficient prima facie materials in the charge sheet to proceed with trial against the accused for the offences punishable u/Sec. 395 of IPC,
charge was framed for the said offences and read over and explained to the accused in the language known to them.
The accused have pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Then, the matter was posted for evidence of the prosecution.
7. In the meantime the accused No.3 remained absent.
Hence, this split up case came to be registered against accused No.3 in SC No. 260/2019.
The trial in original cases was continued.
After full fledged trial case against A1 Vinod and A2 Subramanya was disposed off in SC No. 37/2013 c/w SC No. 376/2015.

10.
All the incriminating evidence appearing against accused in the evidence of P.W.1 to 11 were read over and explained to the accused in the language known to them.
The accused has denied all the incriminating evidence appearing against him.
Accused has submitted that he has no defence evidence.
Hence, the matter was posted for arguments.
11. Heard the arguments of Learned counsel for the accused and Learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the charge sheet, oral and documentary evidence adduced on behalf of the prosecution, written arguments and other materials available on record.

12. Having done so, the following points will arise for my consideration :
S.C.No.260/2019 1. Whether the prosecution proves that on 26.7.2012 at about 1.00 p.m. when the complainant Smt.Saraswathamma was walking at footpath near Dhobi Ghat, 15th Cross, at that came and restrained her and pushed her and thereby, snatched gold Mangalya chain weighing 30 gms from her neck and fled away and thereby the accused have committed the offence punishable u/sec. 395 of IPC?
2.
What Order?

13. My findings on the above points are as under:
 (1) Point No.1 .. In the Negative  (2) Point No.2 .. As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  14. Points No.1 .
The Police Inspector of Vyalikaval police station had filed the charge sheet against the accused alleging the offences punishable u/Sec. 395 of IPC before learned 8th ACMM, Bengaluru.

The allegations made in the charge sheet against the accused are as follows:

sentences.text: On 26.7.2012 at about 1.00 p.m. when the complainant Smt.Saraswathamma was walking at footpath near Dhobi Ghat, 15th Cross, at that time, accused No.1 to 3 along with J-1 & 2 came and restrained her and pushed her and thereby, S.C.No.260/2019 snatched gold Mangalya chain weighing 30 gms from her neck and fled away.
15. The prosecution in order to prove the aforesaid allegations made against the accused had adduced the evidence of 11 witnesses as P.W.1 to 11 and marked 14 documents and 6 MOs.

16. Now let us examine the evidence of aforesaid prosecution witnesses and documents produced on behalf of the prosecution in order to adjudicate whether their evidence is sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubts or not.
17. Smt.Saraswathamma is examined as PW.1.

She has deposed that on 26.7.2012 when she was returning from Baba Temple, and walking at footpath near Dhobi Ghat, 15 th cross at about 12.00 noon, at that time, a person came and restrained her and tried to pull her chain from the neck, she resisted, so he could not take the chain,
thereafter, some 3 persons came from behind and pushed her and she fell down,
thereafter, they snatched Mangalya chain.
She has identified the accused No.3 standing before the court and also stated two other accused persons standing before the court have pushed her from behind.
She also says, apart from these three persons, may be two other persons were present during the incident.
She has identified the complaint and her signature.
Also, identified spot S.C.No.260/2019 mahazar and her signature
which are marked as Exs.P.1, 1(a), 2 and 2(a).
She has identified her signature at Ex.P.2.
She has been subjected to lengthy cross-examination by the defence counsel.

18. PW.2 D.N.Krishnamurthy who is stated to have purchased the stolen property i.e.
a cut piece of mangalya chain.

He says, in the year 2012, in the 7th month, one lady by name Smt.Geetha came to his shop and gave him small cut piece of gold stating that it belongs to her and since her husband is not keeping well, hence, she wanted money, accordingly, he weighed the said chain piece and gave her Rs.23,000/-
(Rupees Twenty three thousand only) and police recovered the same under seizure mahazar.
19. PW.3 Subba Shetty - Archak of Chamundeshwari temple situated behind the Raja Mill, Bangalore.
He has deposed that he is archak by profession in the above said temple.

One year ago, as usual, he performed pooja at temple, thereafter, he noticed some person had put one tali and two kasu in the mangalarathi plate, thereafter one week later, Vyalikaval police came to the temple along with 2 boys and the said boys told about dropping two kasu and one tali in the mangalarathi plate.

At the instance of police, he handed over the said articles to the police and went to the police station,
who have seized the said articles as per seizure mahazar S.C.No.260/2019 Ex.P.4 and Vyalikaval Ps vs A3 Prabhu Alias Pune Alias Kirana on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60600331/

He has not identified the accused No.1 to 3 who were present before the court.
He says, he is not aware of the contents of the seizure mahazar.
20. PW.4 S.Subramanya is one of the spot mahazar witness.
He has identified his signature in the spot mahazar as Ex.P.2(b).

He says, on 26.7.2012, at 5th cross,
Malleshwaram near Dhobi ghat foot path, Vyalikaval police drawn mahazar and seized one pair of hawai chappal, one pair of chappal designed with black sole with blue belt, one rudrakshi chain with black thread, one blue colour saree and the same are identified and marked as MOs.1 to 4.
21. PW.5
Venkatesh

another seizure mahazar witness has deposed that in the year 2012, Vyalikaval police summoned him to the police station and accused No.1 and 3 present before the court were seen in the police station, the police stated their name as Vinod and Prabhu and said they have stolen gold chain and kept near Muneshwara temple and the same requires to be seized and accordingly, requested him to accompany.

So, they all went behind the Muneshwara temple and at the instance of the accused, Archak of the said temple who was in his house, gave one gold tali and two kasu and the same was seized by the police as per seizure mahazar and he has identified his signature as Ex.P.4(c).
S.C.No.260/2019 22.
PW.6 Shabbir who is stated to have caught hold the accused.

He says, in the year 2012 in the month of July at about 12.00 noon, when himself and his friend CW.4 were in their shop, at that time, one old lady was walking in the footpath of 15th cross, at that time, some persons by name Vinod, Pune and 3 others came there and snatched chain from her and started running and they were able to catch hold 2 persons and 3 other persons ran away and they handed over the accused to the police.
On enquiry, they told their name as Vinod and Pune.
He has identified accused No.3 who was present before the court.
Another person ran away is also present before the court who is accused No.1 Vinod.

Smt.Sarala has stated in the year 2012 August month, one boy came to her house and handed over a gold cut piece chain and told that police would leave her brother Manob if she takes the same and police will let of her brother stating so, he ran away.
The said boy did not disclose her who had given the said cut chain to him.
Thereafter, 4 months later, police came along with boy, the said boy told to hand over the cut piece chain to the police, accordingly, she gave the same to the police.
Police seized the same by drawing mahazar as per Ex.P.6 and her signature as Ex.P.6(c).
PW.8 Girish is another seizure witness to Ex.P.3, but he has not supported the case.
Even inspite of treating him as hostile witness, he has not supported.

PW.9 Dr.Veena has stated that she treated PW.1 Smt.Saraswathamma on 26.7.2012 at about 2.15 p.m. for the injuries shown in the medical certificate which is marked as Ex.P.9.
26.
PW.10 B.Jagannatha Rai is police official.
He has stated that on 26.7.2012 at 1.10 p.m. when he was on duty, CW.4 and 6 came along with chain, old lady and 2 persons along with public and handed over the said persons to him.
He noticed the old lady sustained injuries and he sent her to K.C.General Hospital for treatment.

Thereafter, the said lady was again brought before him at the police station, he enquired her and recorded sworn statement in Crime No.118/2012 as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable u/s.395 of IPC and submitted FIR to higher authorities.
He has stated regarding further investigation done by him and seizing the material objects, submission of charge sheet against the accused persons.
27. PW.11 B.P.Nagaraju is Police Inspector.
He has deposed regarding nominating him and other staff by PW.1 to trace out the accused.

Accordingly, on 31.7.2012, he with the S.C.No.260/2019 help of informants found the A1 Vinod @ Bread and brought him to the police station and handed over along with report as per Ex.P.11 before PW.10.

He was also nominated to trace other accused persons and accordingly, with the help of his staff and other informants, he was able to identify the A4 Manob and Rakesh (JCL's) and produced before PW.10.

He was also nominated to trace out the mother of the A1 Smt.Geetha, he along with CWs.15, 16, 19 went in search of her and she was traced around 11.45 a.m. and he produced her before PW.10 along with report as per Ex.P.14.
28.
This court has gone through the oral and material evidence on record.

Even though prosecution is able to examine 11 witnesses out of 22 witnesses, but the evidence of PW.1 complainant-cum-victim is not satisfactory with regard to the identification of the accused persons and also seizure of the material objects.

In the cross-examination she admitted that at the time of lodging the complaint she could not disclose the description of the persons who robbed her chain and she admitted that she do not remember the face of those persons.
No doubt, the prosecution has examined seizure mahazar witnesses, they too have not satisfactorily deposed before the court about seizing of the mangalya chain belonging to PW.1.
Though the prosecution says, the police have recovered cut pieces of mangalya chain, but as stated above, regarding identification of the said property is not satisfactorily identified.
Admittedly, 2 other accused persons are JCL who have been produced before the Juvenile courts.
. The prosecution has been examined one of the eye witness to the alleged incident i.e. Shabbir PW.6.

In the chief examination, he has stated that when himself and CW.4 were at his shop, they noticed an old lady was walking in the 15 th cross foot path, at that time, some 5 persons came there and snatched her chain and they were able to catch 2 persons out of 5 persons and identified accused No.3 standing before the court and also accused No.1 who alleged to have escaped on that day, but in the cross-examination, he has given go-bye to his statement before the court.

On perusal of the evidence of other witnesses i.e. seizure mahazar witness and also spot mahazar witnesses,
even though at certain places, their evidence seem to be supporting to the prosecution case, but if examined their over all evidence that too in the cross- examination, all these witnesses have given Vyalikaval Ps vs A3 Prabhu Alias Pune Alias Kirana on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60600331/
6 go-bye to their version made in the chief examination.

sentences.text: 30. After appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence placed by the prosecution, the prosecution is not able to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
There is contrary version between the witnesses.

On perusal of the over all oral evidence of the witnesses, this court is of the opinion that the prosecution has failed to prove the alleged guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt with cogent, reliable and direct circumstantial evidence as the accused who have committed the alleged offence.
Hence, this court of the opinion that accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt regarding commission of alleged offences.

Accordingly, S.C.No.260/2019 this court is the opinion that the accused No.3 is liable to be acquitted for the offences punishable u/Sec.
395 of IPC.
The prosecution has failed to prove Points No.1.

Accordingly, this court answered Point No.1 in the Negative.
31.
Point No.2:

In view of my findings on points No.1 to 9, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Acting u/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused No.3 Prabhu @ Pune @ Kirana is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable u/Sec. 395 of IPC.
The bail bonds and surety bonds executed by the accused No.3 stands cancelled after appeal period is over.
Office is directed to issue release intimation to release A3 if his custody does not require in any other case.
M.Os.1 to 4 being worthless are ordered to be destroyed after the appeal period is over.
MO. 5 and 6 the gold chain and one tali and two kasu which are released to the complainant as per the deposition of PW. 1 dated 23.10.2013 is made absolute.
